prompt: State one conceptual difference between user-based collaborative filtering and the latent-factor method in Assignment 2.
explanation: User-based filtering derives a prediction from similar users and their centered ratings; latent factors learn low-dimensional user and item vectors whose dot product reconstructs known ratings.
misconception: Check the representation, objective, and scale assumption before committing to an answer.
visualHook: Draw the state transition or data summary before calculating.
accepted: neighbourhood weighted ratings versus dot product of learned factors
solution: They use different representations and prediction mechanisms even when both estimate the same missing entry.

prompt: A new user has no known ratings. Which part of the user-based workflow becomes undefined, and why?
explanation: There is no row mean or similarity evidence for the new user, so a neighbourhood prediction needs a fallback such as a prior, onboarding signal, or item popularity.
misconception: Check the representation, objective, and scale assumption before committing to an answer.
visualHook: Draw the state transition or data summary before calculating.
accepted: row mean and similarity are unavailable
cold start has no ratings for centering or neighbours
solution: The missing evidence is the user profile itself, not merely one missing matrix cell.
